# Extra Data Types Task - Printing a Receipt 

In this task, you will a program to print a paper receipt for the cashier at a small shop.

![](https://thumbs.dreamstime.com/b/people-shop-small-grocery-store-bangkok-thailand-december-people-shop-small-stand-alone-grocery-store-lumpini-park-134483398.jpg?w=500)

For this task you should work together in pairs - you should use [pair programming](https://pxr687.github.io/Intro_Comp_Programming/1_01_Class_Rules.html#pair-programming).

Again, [**DO NOT USE AI TO DO THIS TASK**](https://pxr687.github.io/Intro_Comp_Programming/1_01_Class_Rules.html#ai). If you are new to programming, this task will be quite hard. So, please also ask myself and your TA for help. You will learn a lot more if you do this yourself, with no AI :)

## Instructions

A customer buys six products, and your program should calculate the final bill.

Create variables for:

- Product 1 name and price

- Product 2 name and price

- Product 3 name and price

- Product 4 name and price

- Product 5 name and price

- Product 6 name and price

- Quantity of each product

- Discount percentage (you do not have to do this one, but you can if you want a challenge :) )

- Amount of money the customer pays

Your program should calculate:


- The cost of each product

- The subtotal

- The discount amount (but only if you want to include this)

- The final bill

- The change to give the customer

Finally, `print()` a receipt like this:

```
====== RECEIPT ======

Coffee       2 x ฿40
Sandwich     1 x ฿35
Lemon Cake   2 x ฿47
Chang        2 x ฿15
Pockey       1 x ฿40
Peanuts      2 x ฿40

Subtotal:        ฿359
Discount:        ฿20
Total:           ฿339
Cash:            ฿400
Change:          ฿61

====================
Thank you!
```

**Note**: you should not hard-code your receipt. You should use variables, and `print()` the value of those, together with your text.

**Also note:** there is more than one correct way to do this task...
